stories.headline: Nvidia adds a record $150B to its buyback, lifting remaining authorization to $235B

key_facts.fact: On Sept. 28, 2026, Nvidia's board authorized an additional $150 billion under its existing share repurchase program, raising the total remaining authorization to $235 billion.
key_facts.excerpt: NVIDIA today announced that its Board of Directors has authorized an additional $150 billion under the company's existing share repurchase program, increasing the total remaining amount authorized to $235 billion.

key_facts.fact: Nvidia expects to execute the full remaining program through fiscal year 2028, which ends Jan. 30, 2028, and called it the largest share repurchase authorization increase in history.
key_facts.excerpt: Nvidia said it expects to 'execute' the share buyback plan through its fiscal year that ends in Jan. 30, 2028.

key_facts.fact: The increase eclipses Apple's $110 billion buyback approval in 2024 and exceeds the market capitalization of about 84% of S&P 500 constituents, per LSEG data.
key_facts.excerpt: Nvidia boosted its share buyback authorization by a record US$150 billion, eclipsing Apple's US$110 billion approval in 2024 ... exceeds the market capitalization of about 84 per cent of the S&P 500 constituents, according to data compiled by LSEG.

key_facts.fact: Nvidia ended the July quarter with $22.44 billion in cash and equivalents and last announced an $80 billion buyback in May; its stock trades near its lowest earnings multiple in more than a decade.
key_facts.excerpt: Nvidia ended the July quarter with US$22.44 billion in cash and cash equivalents. It last announced an US$80 billion share buyback in May.

key_facts.fact: Jensen Huang said Nvidia's cash generation gives it capacity to both invest in the AI transition and return capital to shareholders.
key_facts.excerpt: "Our cash generation gives us the capacity to invest in the technologies that advance this transformation and return capital to shareholders. This authorization reflects our confidence in the long-term opportunity ahead."

stories.headline: China signals it will let ByteDance and Alibaba buy Nvidia's new RTX Pro 5500 chips

key_facts.fact: China's Ministry of Industry and Information Technology told some companies, including ByteDance and Alibaba, that it intends to approve purchases of a new Nvidia chip, The Information reported on Sunday, Sept. 27, citing two people familiar with the matter.
key_facts.excerpt: China's Ministry of Industry and Information Technology told some Chinese companies the government intends to approve the purchases, the report added.

key_facts.fact: The chip is the RTX Pro 5500; the ministry asked companies to report how many they want and for what purpose. ByteDance is considering an order of about 1 million chips.
key_facts.excerpt: The ministry, which oversees technology policy, asked companies to report how many chips they wanted and for what purpose ... Sources said ByteDance is considering an order of about 1 million chips.

key_facts.fact: Nvidia plans to ship about 500,000 units per quarter to China starting in late December and told customers to order by Sept. 30; the card sells in China for 85,000-90,000 yuan, similar to Huawei's Ascend 950PR.
key_facts.excerpt: Nvidia plans to ship about 500,000 units per quarter to China starting in late December and has told customers they must order by Sept. 30 to secure supply. The RTX Pro 5500 sells in China for 85,000 to 90,000 yuan ... similar to the price of the Ascend 950PR chip Huawei released earlier this year.

key_facts.fact: Chinese chip stocks fell on Sept. 28 on the report: SMIC lost 3.7%, Moore Threads 6.3% and Cambricon 5.7%.
key_facts.excerpt: Chinese chip stocks fell on Sept. 28: SMIC lost 3.7%, Moore Threads 6.3% and Cambricon 5.7%.

key_facts.fact: Washington has not said whether the RTX Pro 5500 can ship to China; earlier H200 approvals had delivered no chips by May 2026.
key_facts.excerpt: Earlier H200 approvals had delivered no chips by May 2026, and Washington has not said whether the RTX Pro 5500 can ship to China.

key_facts.fact: An Nvidia spokesperson said its China business remains constrained by both U.S. export controls and Beijing's restrictions on American imports.
key_facts.excerpt: An Nvidia spokesperson told the publication that the company's business in China remains constrained by both U.S. export controls and Beijing's restrictions on American imports.

stories.headline: SK Hynix's Solidigm weighs US IPO at up to $150B, which would be the largest chip listing ever

key_facts.fact: SK Hynix's US NAND/SSD unit Solidigm is considering an IPO as early as next year that could value it at up to $150 billion and raise about $15 billion, Reuters reported Sept. 25 citing three people familiar.
key_facts.excerpt: Chipmaker SK Hynix's Solidigm is considering an initial public offering as early as next year that could value the US subsidiary at up to $150 billion ... The company could raise $15 billion in the IPO, the three people said.

key_facts.fact: Solidigm held 'bake-off' pitch meetings with investment banks competing for IPO roles during the week, a concrete step toward what could be the largest-ever US semiconductor listing.
key_facts.excerpt: Solidigm held pitch meetings this week with investment banks competing for roles on the IPO, in a process known as a "bake-off," ... marking a concrete step toward what could become the largest-ever US semiconductor listing.

key_facts.fact: The valuation would far exceed Arm's roughly $54 billion at its 2023 debut and Cerebras' ~$56 billion fully diluted valuation in its 2026 IPO.
key_facts.excerpt: A valuation of up to $150 billion would far exceed recent semiconductor IPOs, including Arm Holdings' roughly $54 billion valuation at its 2023 debut and Cerebras Systems' approximately $56 billion fully diluted valuation in its 2026 IPO.

key_facts.fact: Bloomberg reported the same day that Solidigm could be valued at as much as $100 billion; SK Hynix said nothing specific has been decided.
key_facts.excerpt: Bloomberg reported the same day that Solidigm could be valued at as much as $100 billion ... "Solidigm is reviewing various options to strengthen its business competitiveness, but nothing specific has been decided at this point," SK Hynix said.

key_facts.fact: Solidigm grew out of Intel's NAND and SSD business, which SK Hynix agreed to buy for about $9 billion in 2020; it is also studying a US NAND plant, with upstate New York among possible sites.
key_facts.excerpt: Solidigm grew out of Intel's NAND and solid-state drive business, which SK hynix agreed to ... for about $9 billion in 2020 ... Solidigm is ... building a NAND plant in the US, with upstate New York among the ... sites, Reuters reported earlier this month.

stories.headline: NXP-Vanguard venture VSMC opens its $7.8B Singapore fab, eyes a second plant

key_facts.fact: VisionPower Semiconductor Manufacturing Company (VSMC), the joint venture of Vanguard International Semiconductor (VIS) and NXP, marked the grand opening of its first 300mm fab in Tampines, Singapore on Sept. 28, 2026.
key_facts.excerpt: VisionPower Semiconductor Manufacturing Company Pte. Ltd. (VSMC), the joint venture established in September 2024 by Vanguard International Semiconductor Corporation (VIS...) and NXP Semiconductors N.V. ... today marked the grand opening of its first 12-inch (300mm) fab in Tampines, Singapore.

key_facts.fact: The fab has entered risk production, with volume production scheduled for Q1 2027; its first sample lot achieved yields above 99% after 22 months of construction.
key_facts.excerpt: the fab has entered the risk production stage, with volume production scheduled to begin in the first quarter of 2027 ... Following 22 months of construction, the fab successfully processed its first sample lot, achieving yields above 99%

key_facts.fact: The fab supports 130nm to 40nm processes for mixed-signal, power management, analog and interposer chips, and will produce about 44,000 12-inch wafers a month at full capacity by 2029, creating about 1,600 jobs.
key_facts.excerpt: The fab will support process technologies ranging from 130nm to 40nm for mixed-signal, power management, analog, and interposer applications ... At full capacity by 2029, the fab is expected to produce approximately 44,000 12-inch wafers per month, create around 1,600 jobs

key_facts.fact: The fab cost US$7.8 billion; VIS is about 19% owned by TSMC, and VSMC chairman Leuh Fang said the company is considering a second plant in Singapore, expecting the AI-driven chip shortage to last longer.
key_facts.excerpt: The US$7.8 billion (S$10.5 billion) fab in Tampines Wafer Park ... VIS ... is about 19% owned by ... TSMC ... Leuh Fang, VSMC chairman, told the media that the company is also considering a second plant in Singapore to meet growing chip demand. The chip supply shortage amid the AI boom is likely to last longer, he said.

key_facts.fact: NXP CEO Rafael Sotomayor called the venture NXP's largest investment since it acquired Freescale Semiconductor in 2015, pitching it as supply for 'physical AI' systems.
key_facts.excerpt: NXP's Sotomayor said the joint venture is one of the most significant milestones in the company's decades-long history in Singapore, and its largest investment since it acquired Freescale Semiconductor in 2015.

stories.headline: Physical-AI chip startup SiMa.ai raises $150M at a $1.45B valuation

key_facts.fact: SiMa.ai, which develops chips and software letting robots, drones, cameras and other devices run AI on-device, raised a $150 million Series C at a $1.45 billion valuation, co-led by Fidelity and Amplify.
key_facts.excerpt: SiMa.ai, a startup developing chips and software that allow robots, drones, cameras, and other devices to run AI directly on the device, has raised a $150 million Series C at a $1.45 billion valuation. The round was co-led by Fidelity Management & Research Company and Amplify

key_facts.fact: Total capital raised is now over $500 million; the startup was valued at $960 million after an $85 million Series B in July 2025, per PitchBook.
key_facts.excerpt: The new round brings SiMa.ai's total capital raised to over $500 million. The startup was previously valued at $960 million after raising an $85 million ... B in July ... 025, according to PitchBook.

key_facts.fact: New investors AllianceBernstein, Baron Capital, J.P. Morgan and the State of Michigan joined; Dell Technologies Capital, Point72 and StepStone also participated.
key_facts.excerpt: with participation from Alter Venture Partners, Dell Technologies Capital, Maverick Capital, +ND Capital, Point72, and StepStone Group. AllianceBernstein, Baron Capital, J.P. Morgan, and the State of Michigan also joined the round as new investors.

key_facts.fact: The money funds a third-generation platform, with a flagship targeting 1,000 TOPS of compute at 80 watts in the first half of 2028, for drones, humanoid robots and automotive ADAS.
key_facts.excerpt: its flagship offering targeted to deliver 1,000 tera operations per second (TOPS) of compute at 80 watts. Slated for the first half of 2028, the platform will include ML IP, chiplets and SoCs for drones, humanoid robots, automotive ADAS and AI-powered cockpits.

key_facts.fact: SiMa.ai positions itself against Nvidia GPUs, which it describes as expensive and power-hungry for physical AI.
key_facts.excerpt: While Physical AI has historically relied on expensive, complex, and power-hungry NVIDIA GPUs, SiMa.ai delivers the industry's leading full-stack Physical AI platform

stories.headline: Anthropic commits $11.6B over seven years to Akamai cloud CPUs, gets warrant for up to 5%

key_facts.fact: Akamai announced on Sept. 24, 2026 an $11.6 billion, seven-year contractual commitment from Anthropic to support Anthropic's CPU workload demands on Akamai Cloud.
key_facts.excerpt: Akamai Technologies, Inc. (NASDAQ: AKAM), today announced a significantly expanded relationship with Anthropic for $11.6 billion of contractual commitment over seven years. The multi-year commitment will support Anthropic's accelerating CPU workload demands

key_facts.fact: The deal can expand by up to $9 billion more, to about $20 billion; Akamai issued Anthropic a warrant for up to ~5% of its common stock at $111.33 per share, with about 2% vesting on the initial commitment and 1% per additional $3 billion.
key_facts.excerpt: potential expansion of the relationship by up to an additional $9 billion, which represents a total potential commitment of approximately $20 billion ... up to approximately 5% of Akamai's common stock outstanding, at an exercise price of $111.33 per share ... Each additional $3 billion purchase of cloud services ... will result in the vesting of approximately 1%

key_facts.fact: Akamai estimates about $5.5 billion in total capex tied to the commitment, including an extra ~$1.7 billion in 2026 to pre-purchase supply-chain components such as memory.
key_facts.excerpt: Total capital expenditures related to today's $11.6 billion commitment are estimated to be approximately $5.5 billion ... an increase of approximately $1.7 billion in capital expenditures in 2026 to secure and pre-purchase critical supply chain components, including memory.

key_facts.fact: The deal is more than six times a $1.8 billion Anthropic-Akamai deal reported in May, is the largest in Akamai's history and the first to include a warrant; the commitment depends on Akamai meeting delivery and availability requirements.
key_facts.excerpt: That's more than six times the size of a $1.8 billion deal between the two companies that Bloomberg reported in May. The commitment isn't ironclad; according to Akamai's securities filing, it depends on Akamai meeting certain delivery and service-availability requirements

key_facts.fact: Akamai shares rose as much as 17% in late trading, to $129.60, after the announcement.
key_facts.excerpt: Akamai shares rose as much as 17% in late trading, to $129.60, according to Bloomberg.

stories.headline: Cipher Digital lands a $5.2B, 10-year lease extension at its Texas data center from an AI lab

key_facts.fact: On Sept. 25, 2026, Cipher Digital said it amended its Barber Lake lease with Fluidstack and signed a binding commitment with an unnamed 'leading AI lab' for a separate 10-year lease after Fluidstack's term, extending the contracted term from 10 to 20 years.
key_facts.excerpt: Cipher has executed an amendment to its existing lease with Fluidstack ... coupled with a binding commitment with a leading AI lab to lease the facility for an additional 10-year term following the conclusion of the Barber Lake Lease.

key_facts.fact: The new lease adds about $5.2 billion of contracted revenue, lifting total contracted revenue at the Colorado City, Texas site from $3.8 billion to over $9 billion.
key_facts.excerpt: extend the contracted lease duration of its Barber Lake data center in Colorado City, Texas from 10 years to 20 years and increase total contracted revenue at the facility from $3.8 billion to over $9 billion.

key_facts.fact: Data halls are now due between Q4 2026 and Q1 2027; Cipher bears the first $359.3 million of cost overruns, with the tenant reimbursing 50% of costs above that over the 20-year term.
key_facts.excerpt: individual data halls now expected to be delivered between the fourth quarter of 2026 and the first quarter of 2027 ... the Company will bear the first $359.3 million of costs in excess of the initial budgeted amount ... The tenant will reimburse the Company over the aggregate twenty-year term for 50% of any such costs above that amount

key_facts.fact: Barber Lake is a 300 MW site; Cipher now has 700 MW of gross capacity under contract for $16.5 billion in revenue, including two AWS sites.
key_facts.excerpt: Cipher now has 700 MW of gross capacity under contract for $16.5 billion in revenue. In addition to the Fluidstack deal, these contracts include 100 MW for Amazon Web Services at its Stingray site and 300 MW for AWS at its Black Pearl site
